TL:DR. Great game. Small amount of jank. Optimisation is not great, and a level of improvement is needed. Upscaling is basically a crutch. Building is really fun. All in all, I would say its worth giving it a try. 

Fun game with good progression systems and stuff to level up. The building mechanic is really cool, and I loved the way bug corpses become obstructions that you might have to destroy. Getting surrounded with piles of bug corpses will obstruct building, closing gates, and escape routes forcing you to climb over them. They can be burned or melee'd to dispose of them. 
Building has a good amount of depth. The closest comparison I can think of is Fortnite Save the World. I find you want to build in sections so if the bugs make it in, you can fall back to the next section. 

My negative critisms are. 
Upscaling is a heavy crutch for optimization. While the games graphics are good enough in my opinion. They aren't anything groundbreaking, yet the hardware usage is very high in comparison. Even the menu uses a ton of GPU? A performance update would be nice. 
The game has some jank. Nothing game breaking to my knowledge. Just a few things feel a bit uncomfortable. Like climbing ladders, or being in the ship during take off.

Good game to play with some buddies, just not something you will play for long term. More cons than pros, and it is mostly carried by the fact that it is Starship Troopers. My two biggest complaints is how aggressively dark it is, you can't see a damn thing, and there is no way to remedy this issue. the second one is that it feels rather clunky, which is rather disappointing

There is some damn good stuff here. The whole persistent corpses, bugs climbing over their dead, building and defending your base from hordes of bugs down to the shooting. All of this is dang good. In fact I'd even say pretty much all the core gameplay is good.

However, where it unfortunately starts to suffer is when you realise how janked together with spit and glue this game is.
It's very clearly built off of Squad's codebase, another game I have sunken a few hundred hours into

This means this game has some nasty problems
For 1. It's inherited Squad's poor performance, but ten times worse because it's somehow even worse in terms of optimization. If I were to guess, the whole issue is the amount of enemies being rendered on screen and the persistent corpses. I wouldn't sacrifice these mechanics for better performance but I do hope we get some better optimization in other places to loosen the bottleneck a bit
2. It's JANK in several places, from a number of bugs (And not the kind you can shoot) to just overall weirdness in some aspects (Why does the Engineer's mobile build tool ability have an 80 second cooldown???)
3. What's up with the weird company system and why is the new planet locked to it?
4. The game feels pretty poorly explained in terms of some mechanics so it can leave noobs wondering what the heck to do


Either way. The game is an enjoyable time and really does channel the spirit of Starship Troopers at it's peak moments, but you should expect a bumpy, windy road getting to those peak moments.

If I could recommend a "maybe" for this game I would. It's not a bad game, but after about 10 multiplayer missions you've pretty much seen everything the game has to offer. I don't even bother playing on hard because the bugs kill you pretty much instantly and they are bullet sponge tanks. I played as a grenadier for the entire time I've played except a few missions as heavy gunner. I would say the grenade launcher feels pretty good (although very inaccurate). The rest of the guns felt extremely weak to me. I wish they would make the guns feel stronger and give you more variety in your loadout because right now the bugs are much stronger than your weapons and your loadout choices are pretty limited per class (unless you grind a ton and rank up forever).

Playing as a explosives guy, I had a lot of issues placing remote bombs. I don't know if it was the server lag, but in the middle of combat sometimes my bombs just wouldn't place on the ground and I'd end up dying because I couldn't deploy my bombs. Kind of glitchy and frustrating. Just let us throw the bomb packs out instead of placing directly on a spot.

The base building is pretty good, but your defenses are fairly paper-thin when going up against the hordes. I would say they need to boost the defenses a little bit also. Most missions just devolve into everyone running around on fire and you not being able to see what's going on. The giant yellow tanks are insanely tanky, they killed me pretty much everytime and sometimes come in groups. Kind of annoying unloading 12 grenade rounds, 2 remote packs, and multiple hand gun rounds into it and not killing it.

I do feel a bit like the DLC is a cash-grab for skins & gun colors. Not really worth it in my opinion when you don't even really see your own character and most of the levels are pretty dark.

The solo missions are near unplayable. I got through about 4 and then just gave up on them. I dropped a canister I was carrying extremely far and it just disappeared. I wasn't about to run back the entire way for another (for the 3rd time). I would just stick to the tutorial and then straight to multiplayer to avoid frustration.

Matchmatching is a bit of a problem right now. It takes several minutes to find a server and you won't be able to really pick the exact mission type you want. You will eventually connect, but it's just totally random what server & game mode you get.

Overall, it was a fun nostalgic way to re-live the movie and play base horde for a while, but there are some problems with this game that make it not as fun as it could be. I wouldn't say it's a bad game at all, but needs improvement for more replay. It seems like the devs are actively working on it though, so I hope they make it better.

Despite everyone telling me that I should hate this game, I simply cannot do it. Sure, it’s not amazing, but I’d give it a lukewarm recommendation for a few key reasons. 

I have seen performance improvements over time. A few months back, I considered a refund after the performance was so bad on my mid-range rig with an i7-9800 and a RTX 2060. But I stuck around and through both my tweaking of the settings and performance related patches, it now performs quite well. 

I genuinely enjoy the big team PvE feel. It feels fun when I am on a team of 16 mobile infantrymen holding the line against a horde of bugs. Base building is fun and adds a unique gameplay mechanic. I love playing the Assault and Secure game type and seeing what whacky base designs my team can throw together. Repairing and resupplying during Horde mode waves is frantic and fun.

I like the classes! There is truly something for everyone, from support to DPS, pick a class and get to extermination. My chief complaint of the class system is that there is just not enough progression! At around 12 hours, I completed the engineer class and I wish there was more to unlock and do.

The bugs are fun and fighting is hectic! I love how dead bug create piles that can be utilized by living bugs to climb up and scale the walls. Gunplay is so-so, but its good enough. Bug variety is good and I hope to see more. The tiger bugs sound annoying  af though.

Comparisons of this game and Helldivers 2 are natural, but I’d argue that they are misplaced. The tight 4 player loadout based PvE of Helldivers is very different than the big team 16 player class based PvE that Starship Troopers offers. Both are good! 

I get it, some have legit complaints about the game. But as Marge Simpson said “I just think they're neat!” I cannot argue with myself about the fun I have playing this game, and I hope it continues to be supported and made better. TLDR; A game that may be worth keeping an eye on, worth buying for £30 or £40 but requires improvement to become and stay competitive.

It sort of reminds me of early BF4, it has to look like arse (ass for those across the pond) in order to run, plays like arse at times, has it's own bug infestation (ironically), and has a couple of crappy game mechanics; namely the company system (more on this later), yet has a good game design at its core as well as a great sound (bar a couple of bugs) to it, and most importantly massive potential. 

Looks wise, it is decent. Higher resolutions and high settings will cause serious performance issues (even the NASA computer kids on reddit have problems), yet it still looks decent enough (and is immersive enough) on the necessary settings (namely 2560-1440 res, ultra performance balancing, low everything bar medium texture) that it doesn't cause me any major issues for long-term game enjoyment. 

Play wise it works well overall, there are some bugs that may cause a slight freeze (although I suspect it is more performance issues than anything, especially when the flammenwerfer comes out to play), sometimes the sound can bug out when rapid firing HMG emplacements, and there is the occasional crashing to menu/desktop. yet to be fair these are fairly rare (past dozen or so games it crashed once at the end of a performance intensive match). Overall it is great to play, especially due to the seemingly innovative and very fun decision to not despawn bodies and add physics and mass to them, filling a corridor at the end of a 10 wave horde fight is incredibly fun, especially in urban maps.

It's biggest issue by far though is the company system. It's (as others have pointed out) obviously a clone of the helldivers system, the issue is that unless you start your own company (and have 30 mates willing to play it with you at set times) you will likely have problems with it. Either because they (a company) don't want new players (level up is reasonably fast but shouldn't make a difference), are holding a spot for somebody else, can't be bothered to deal with sorting through join requests, or just simply aren't active. Whilst it doesn't stop you from playing, it does look as though there are certain rewards (and possibly a storyline of sorts) that you can't obtain. 

Personally I would have said the best way forwards was to scrap the need for being in a company (have it like Holdfast's and most other games clan/regiment systems (even war thunder has it's squadrons reasonably sorted on issues like this)), and have it so there is an overarching series of grand campaigns (as with Helldivers) you can join, either as a squad (of up to 25 people), regiment (of up to 50), battalion (of up to 100), or a division (up to 200), with the opportunity for larger armies if someone really cares enough to try and herd a playerbase like that (personally I would rather herd cats). Have it so players can either join a group on a more permenant basis or simply play with random squads/groups rather than having to group up. It could be fun to have an overarching campaign where players actions (especially the larger groups) influence the outcome and state of the galaxy as a whole, win or lose like in old (I won't touch the new with a barge-pole) BF2.  

Overall it is a fun game to play, I wouldn't pay more than forty quid, but I suspect (or hope perhaps) that it is going to be a game that sees some very interesting development. Should they go down the line of overarching opt in or out large scale campaigns/events, bug squashing, concept optimisation, and NON-DLC weapons and kit development this has some good potential, so long as the developers don't simply use it as a cash-cow. It seems like a bit of a labour of love (at its core at least) and like I said, is very reminiscent of early BF4 in that it has a rough-ish start but could skyrocket to become a much loved classic, definitely worth watching for now.

However, it is severely lacking in some departments, with my main complaint being the lack of weapon choices.

The different abilities on the 6 different classes were cool, I especially loved the jetpack on the ranger, or the "hunker-down" ability of the "tank". 

The game looks and handles great on my win11 PC, and I have not run into any bugs I could not shoot away yet. 

One suggestion I have, is to have more varied difficulty levels. I am still new to the game, so I play on Easy/normal. However, choosing easy difficulty does not always mean it will be easy - meaning that depending on which kind of mission you choose, you will either get overrun if not careful on Easy, OR not see an enemy with 2 minutes interval because the mission only spawns 2-4 bugs at the time for 16 players.

Been a fan of Starship Troopers franchise since 20 years ago, and I am overjoyed there's finally a fun and enjoyable FPS game that has you fighting for the Federation! The only good bug is a DEAD bug! Except...there's a lot of a bugs. A LOT of bugs. I feel obligated to leave a review because I love this game, but I'm also praying the devs will do good and polish it up. I REALLY want this game to succeed!

The game is great no doubt, with some excellent mechanics such as bug corpses piling up! However, as fun as it is, in the current state (v0.8.0 I think) the game is extremely buggy, unstable, and poorly optimised. Here's the dirty bits:

- Bugs can appear out of nowhere, and disappear into nowhere. They might suddenly phase through rocks, or suddenly zip into the sky and across the map.
- Enemy animations are clunky. Compared to something like Helldivers 2, the animations and physics in this game are pretty atrocious. It feels extremely buggy. For instance, you can be shooting at a load of bugs at the base of a wall, then suddenly, there's a giant Tiger bug glitching out right next to you on the tiny platform. I know it's EA so hopefully all this will be cleaned up in the future, but it does detract from the experience.
- Chaos. Absolute chaos, especially when there are a few grenadiers on your team, and then the bug grenadiers and inferno bugs come out, and all hell breaks loose. You can't see anything for all the FX flaring up around you and the screen shakes like it's having a seizure. I get that the bug war is chaotic, but from a gameplay perspective it is annoying as hell. highly recommend dumbing down the FX a bit.
- The building mechanic is fun, but it HIGHLY depends on how good the team is. A good team will lay out a decent base and try not to waste resource. More often than not though, people will build a bad base with holes here and there, and turn it into a maze where you'll get easily trapped in. Especially annoying during the frantic scramble to evacuate to the EZ, but you're stuck trying to get past the crappy wall layout because the climbing mechanic is so inaccurate. But that's what happens when randos in multiplayer can do whatever they want.
- Optimisation. It's bad. My rig is pretty decent and I can run most games with 0 issues. Yet ST:E crashes often, seizes up often, lags often, and drops framerate like it's fresh outta the oven. It's great work the devs have done already to get so many enemies on screen at once and have the lingering corpse mechanic, but damn. This game needs optimising bad.
- Limited gamemodes. The roadmap says galaxy war is coming and solo content as well which is amazing! But as it is, there are only like 2 real mission types. And Horde mode is extremely buggy.
- Unlockables are hit and miss and needs some rethinking. Some items are invaluable like the deployable stim and ammo packs. Others, like the Hi-Ex Grenade is practically useless. It doesn't throw until a couple of seconds after the key is pressed, and with the glitchy nature of enemy movement, you'll end up sticking it to nothing, coupled with the long grenade cooldown, it's an expensive waste in a desperate fight.

There are a plethora of other issues still needing a lot of attention before I can call this game anywhere near to polished, especially considering the other similar games out on the market. However, the fact that I would still recommend it shows what a great effort the devs have made so far. They've definitely got the vibe of exterminating the arachnids with good ol' lead down to a T. I hope and believe that the devs will pull through and really make this game fantastic. Oh and BTW Offworld, PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE consider redoing the music! The original score of the movie may be locked behind crappy legal walls, but I truly believe the music can be better in pumping the player up to fight more bugs. As is, it's a little flat and boring.

But, remember Civilian! Service guarantees Citizenship! Enlist today and become a Hero of the Federation!

Starship Troopers: Extermination is a thrilling and action-packed co-op first-person shooter that features intense, large-scale battles against relentless alien hordes. Inspired by the 1997 film, the game perfectly captures its chaotic energy and sci-fi atmosphere. Whether you're defending a crumbling wall with your squad or fighting your way to a last-minute extraction, every match feels like a scene from a blockbuster. The immersive visuals and sound design, which include bug screeches, heavy weapon fire, and mission updates from General Rico himself, bring every moment to life. It's more than just shooting bugs; it's a full-scale war.

The game is fundamentally based on teamwork. Players can choose from six distinct classes: Sniper, Ranger, Demolisher, Guardian, Engineer, and Medic, each with their own set of tools and abilities on the battlefield. This class system promotes genuine cooperation, as success is dependent on working together, covering flanks, healing teammates, and constructing defenses under pressure. The base-building element provides significant strategic depth. While under attack, players can gather resources, build walls, deploy turrets, and manage repairs. It transforms every mission into a hybrid of tower defense and fast-paced FPS, keeping the game play interesting and tactical.

The Carnage System is a standout feature, in which fallen Bug bodies accumulate and change the terrain in real time. Enemies can climb over these corpses to get past defenses, forcing players to constantly adapt. With changing objectives, evolving hive threats, and diverse environments, each mission presents new challenges and rewards creative problem-solving. It's also worth noting that the developers are constantly updating the game. Patches, new content drops, and community feedback integration demonstrate that this title is alive and well, with an exciting road map ahead.

Extermination has received consistent praise from Steam users for its intense cooperative game play, dynamic battles, and replay value. Whether you're in public lobbies or playing with friends, the camaraderie and chaos make each session unique. While the single-player mode serves primarily as a narrative introduction, the true magic occurs in multiplayer, where quick decisions, class synergy, and creative defenses can mean the difference between survival and annihilation.

Star ship Troopers: Extermination is a dynamic, ever-changing game that combines large-scale alien warfare with teamwork, strategy, and cinematic chaos. It's a must-play for fans of sci-fi shooters and co-op, and it's only getting better over time. Active game with short Que times. Love it!!!!

Deeper impressions are that this game is actually a great deal of fun. It seems pretty clear this is a AA budget game with devs who are pushing every penny to try and make a horde combat experience that can beat the best AAAs in it's core gameplay design.

Thousands of bugs with a nice amount of variants (Inferno bugs, Grenadier bugs, Gunner bugs, Tanky bugs, little minion bugs etc) that can ambush you at any point. Really flexible base building and good objective based modes that mean you have to leave the safety of your base with little skirmish teams to get resources to build the base more. This experience is actually really close to how you would imagine the movies to feel.

The moment I fell in love with this game truly felt like a movie. It was me and some random medic were on our way to nuke a hive that the rest of the team were ignoring. We didn't have mics on to talk to each other (if it was real you'd probably not want to talk around these bugs anyway). We just understood it was a necessary mission even if we would not make it back to base. We managed to nuke the hive but got ambushed on the way out. We found ourselves backed into a little crevice that was too small for the hundreds of bugs chasing us to get into but we were desparately running out of ammo and nobody was coming. So we were stuck waiting for death or an opening to escape with only a bullet or 2 left in our pistols. What an experience! It actually felt like one of those movie scenes where you hope the main characters get out but there's an ominous sense of doom.

So really, give the game time to grow on you. Take time to experience these fantastic moments. You will get past the rough edges of a AA budget and find a gaming experience that is really intense and actually immersive into the Starship Troopers universe.

I bought the game in early access, I'd say it has paid itself by now in terms of entertainment value, but It had it's flaws like most EA titles. There are situations that really gets your blood pumping, but most of the time it is pretty frustrating. The only really viable way to amass some decent XP and fast leveling is through the game mode "Horde", and it gets pretty monotonous after a while. The worst bits are when your team is wiped out but the piles of corpses are so huge that the bugs themselves can't really find a way through the carnage and finish your HQ off, resulting in you quitting the game and recieving no XP whatsoever. This has happened several times by now.

The lack of players really shows sometimes (but I hope this will get sorted out with 1.0 and X-platform), with zero medics present most of the time the games get really hard, and to be honest, quite annoying. You can't really turn the tide as a lone wolf either.

As I suspected the active player base grew with the 1.0 patch, although it seems the game still struggles to fill 16 players for each game, either that or some or many of them gets kicked due to the current optimization issues, however these are issues which I am yet to enocunter for some reason as mentioned earlier. This makes finishing any match significantly harder than it should be, since you know, you're simply outgunned.

It was actually better before 1.0 as many have stated. The new "content" is locked behind companies, which really doesn't make any sense at all. Clans being all cool and all but really, even with a company there is rarely enough players online to do anything of real value.

As it stands, the game has way too many problems that weren't there just a few days ago.

The biggest issue is the bugged out bug counter in Horde (my favourite game mode, and I bet many others agree), which was the only viable way to gather some decent XP. The piles of corpses may look cool but in fact (I really don't have any performance issues btw, and no crashing problems) it makes the game more or less unplayable. You simply can't kill enough of 'em and unless you're blessed with a max level demolisher you can't even see what you're shooting at after wave 6 or something. To claim a victory on hard difficulty is now near impossble. On normal difficulty it more or less requires each and every player to amass 400+ (a number which is damn near impossible on low ranks) kills to even be remotely close to a win. It's gotten ridicilous.

Add to that, the early wave spawn sometimes happening right after another wave for some reason, where you don't even get 5 seconds to repair the base, come on! Give us a break.

Flamethrower is not working as intended, several weapons are reported that they don't register hits. The flamethrower is especially problematic, because this is where I actually encounter one of the few severe bugs I've heard of, and that's because whenever I use it it completely blackens my screen. I can see tracked bugs through the blackness but that's it. It takes a while before it wears off, it's comparable to being flashed in Counter-Strike, although the effect takes way longer to wear off. If this is an intended mechanic, it really is weird to say the least.

I've been getting stuck in walls and under things in general upon revival plenty of times, not nice.

I once got stuck in a pile of corpses and got 50+ kills with the knife from within the pile, as I was out of ammo i just kept swinging, but the bugs couldn't even touch me, and I couldn't get out. Let that sink in. So stupid, really.

I sacrificed myself as a Demolisher, resulting in a perma death and I couldn't spawn again the wave after, resulting in me sitting in the viewing screen for 45 minutes because the team was unable to finish the game (again, due to the broken bug counter), and the bugs had died in such numbers close to the HQ that they couldn't damage it either (again). There is just no way this mechanic is working as intended? Or am I wrong? Seems to be VERY player unfriendly if that's the case. Also, half the team was gone again, due to disconnects and other various issues.

I mean, I can go on, but what does it matter?

I hope they fix most of these game breaking bugs ASAP or they'll lose most of the player base within a week, I am not kidding here. I loved the game even with it's pre-1.0 flaws but this patch has got even me wondering why I'm still queueing up for this unstable insanity. No matter how much I love shooting stuff, it's really hard to recommend this in its current state.

With that said, as a 80's kid and a vivid fan of the movies, this really is what I've been waiting for for what seems like an eternity. I recommend it, but at the sime time, I don't. 

With it's current pricing, you really should think twice before you spend your money on this. Anything above 29.99 and you really should keep your wallet closed until further notice. But if you got money to spend and is an earlier fan of the franchise you really won't be disappointed either. Just keep an open mind and enjoy the ride. Perhaps your monetary investment can make a difference in the long term, allowing the devs to make this game truly enjoyable, because it really does have promise. Keep in mind, that many great games have been in a terrible state upon launch and have gotten better and better as time goes by.

Grenades cleared the way as we moved deeper, the mission to destroy one hive. Explosions echoed, and the bugs screeched, but our focus never wavered.

On the ice plains of Rho-Tau, the 1st MI skills were tested to the limit. The cold bit through our armor, and the bugs had adapted, moving with terrifying speed across the frozen landscape. But our determination was a fire that no ice could quench. I fought like a veteran, each encounter adding to my growing legend.

The words of my training sergeant echoed in my mind: “Service guarantees citizenship.” But it was more than that. It was about survival, brotherhood, and a fierce determination to protect humanity.

Rangers and Assault units bring mobility and versatility, with tools for close-quarters combat, bug scanning, or long-range sniping. [h1] ST:E - A Flawed Gem In Need Of Polish [/h1]

[h2] This will be a slightly longer review. What is there to be said about ST:E that hasn't already been covered by the various, mixed reviews? I've put over 800 hours into this game (as of the time of this review) and have to say I still have mixed feelings, though I lean more towards a positive outlook, considering I am still playing the game fairly regularly. I can also say, without a doubt, that playing ST:E with a Discord group (the Joint Space Force) has made the experience immensely more enjoyable.

I will break down the things that I love about this game, as well as the things that I, well, [i] put up with.[/i][/h2]


[h3] [b] What I love: [/b] [/h3] 
[*] The core gameplay - The gameplay loop, game modes, classes, weapons, etc.
The game's core gameplay, set within a universe I love, has managed to keep me coming back for more. The weapons are fun to experiment with, the game modes allow you to change things up depending on what you feel like doing, the classes are unique enough that you can get a pretty decent amount of depth from them, and the perks and utilities make it possible to tailor your classes to your playstyle without feeling exploitable or cheap. The mutator system helps to keep things feeling fresh, so much so that playing without them can often feel too easy or boring by comparison. The challenge of dealing with ambushes or random hordes while trying to gather resources during ARC can be challenging and fun, forcing you to adapt from both a micro and macro level, lest you run out of tickets and fail the mission.

[*] 16-Player PvE
Having so many players working together (well, usually) can be ridiculously fun. It leaves many opportunities to make friends or meet cool/memorable players. I was lucky enough to find a Discord group known as the Joint Space Force rather early on in my ST:E career and this really boosted the amount of enjoyment I got out of this game. I have made [i] many [/i] friends from [i] many [/i] backgrounds that have only served to make the game [i] that [/i] much more enjoyable to play. Having people you can joke and screw around with really adds to the experience of getting ran through and shooting Bugs.

[*] The Arachnid Threat
The Bugs of ST:E are really cool; I can't help but feel like the design and behavior of the Bugs are just about spot-on. There are complaints to be made about the little details, such as how Warriors and Drones may get stuck on geometry or clip partially into the ground, but that's to be expected from time to time. Admittedly, it probably happens too often to really defend, but there is a lot of potential here.

The Tigers and big and imposing, leaving your with a strange mix of contempt and respect, almost like a respectable rival that you trade blows with. Sometimes you win, but sometimes you lose. The Grenadier commands a comical, but deadly threat, They're big and blue, leaving a distinct impression that sticks out among the earthy colors of the Bugs and can lead to some hilarious (and frustrating) situations when you're blown halfway across the map . Gunners  have a distinct glow and rotund shape that will become the bane of your existence if you aren't able to adapt and improve. They often act like a positioning skill-check for new or ignorant players and command a unique presence on the battlefield.The addition of Bombadiers has been both a frustrating and entertaining experience because of their small size and incredible jump. I've had some great times both watching and being the target of Bombadier ambushes that lead to joining Fleet in orbit.

Last, but not least, the Warrior Bug. The iconic design and ferocity of the Warriors walk a fine line between being too tanky and too squishy. Almost every game can make the Warriors feel like a unique threat, based on your current objectives, class, weapons, etc. A worthy adversary (most of the time) that are the bread-and-butter of the Bug army. They feel good to shoot, generally speaking, and provide a interesting, ever-changing experience while on the battlefield. I hope you learn to love their 1-shot charge attack on Hard difficulty, otherwise you are really going to hate these guys. (Ha)

[h3] [b] What I loathe: [/b] [/h3]
[*] The various bugs (lowercase 'B')
I have played a lot of different iterations of this game over the past year, including: An engine swap, various buffs and nerfs, class revamps, weapon and perk releases, class tweaks, mechanic revamps, etc. Every update has been accompanied by their own new, or even altered, bugs. The worst have consistently been related to the performance of the game. From crashes and frame drops to servers closing and intense rubberbanding, we've experienced it all. If I had to pick a runner-up for worst bugs, it would have to be the comms. For months we've had to deal with issues of voice chat completely breaking and getting [b] 0 [/b] voice comms, mics constantly on, some players not being heard by others, and push-to-talk becoming a toggle (leading to 'hot mic-ing'), and rendering cooperation almost impossible outside of using text chat, something that is difficult in a PvE game with hundreds of enemies and fast-paced action. Other gripes include equipment causing crashes, being unable to respawn, deployables breaking Bug AI, Bugs spawning in walls and geometry, attachments not working/loading, getting stuck in 3rd person, being unable to use any inputs, being unable to climb/mantle, stuttering while jumping, etc. .etc. .etc. .No, seriously. The list just goes on and on. . .

[*] Development
OWI has made an awesome game, from an awesome IP, with awesome features. BUT. Much of the content has felt half-baked on arrival. With the 1.0 launch we're been unable to get much use from the new Company system due to the exclusion of what could be deemed as standard QOL features, such as invites for friends or a search bar for finding a specific Company. The Carnage system has been really cool, but I'm sure I can vouch for many of the other Early Access players when I say we'd much rather have the game in a stable, smooth state before adding [i] new [/i] content to the mix. Many of the major issues with the game have taken far too long to be ironed-out while we're trying to play the game we've come to enjoy with our friends. It's only been made worse by consistent crashes. It really kills the desire to play the game when your game crashes, making you lose out on all of the experience you've earned, only to find out the Devs would rather roll out their new Bug corpse system or switch to a new game engine.

[*] Rushed launch
Those of us that have been playing ST:E in early access have been holding out hope to see the game become the best it can be. We've hoped and prayed that the 1.0 launch would be the saving grace for the dwindling numbers of players that have left due to the instability and bugginess we've been experiencing for months, but deep down, many of us knew the game would not be ready by the announced release date. The combination of low player count mixed with a shoddy launch could very well kill the game's reputation and, if the mixed reviews are anything to go off of, it seems our fears have been confirmed. We want the game to succeed, but we knew the game just wasn't ready for 1.0 launch, especially to the console market

[h3] [b] In Summary [/b] [/h3]
ST:E has (had?) a lot of potential. A combination of various issues has plagued this game since day 1 and growth has been slow, but there is a lot to love here if you are a nerd who loves the Starship Troopers franchise or if you can laugh and have fun with your friends in a fun, yet flawed game. The gameplay is cool, the Bugs are awesome, and the large team make for a fun experience if you can manage to play with some friends. There are many issues that need to be addressed here and, so far, we don't have a definite answer for whether or not ST:E will be here to stay.

If you like wide-scale community-driven co-op action with expansive buildcrafting and powerful metaprogression this is a game you don't want to miss. 

[h2] Wide scale: 16~20 players [/h2] 
Broken up into 4 player squads.


[h2] Community-Driven: The Galactic Front [/h2] 
The Galactic Front is like a global main objective which changes every major content drop. 

Join/Make a company, complete Company Operations (in other words join missions on the SPARTA), earn Victory Points which translate to global Galactic Front progress. 

When we've made enough progress, we start earning perks and cosmetics. 

So far the playerbase has unlocked 9 perks which everyone even new players can use, on any class, with 3 more on the way for this current sparta campaign.


[h2] Co-op Action: Gamemodes [/h2] 
Advance and Secure: Capture points, kill bug. Rinse repeat. Then run for evac!

ARC defense: Obtain materials to build and defend a base. Manage side objectives. Power up the cave scanner, hold them back, then run for evac!

Horde: 10 waves of bugs each harder than the last. Build a base and fight together to the end. Then run for evac!

Hive Hunt: Nuke bug holes. Then run for evac!

Critical Strike: Fight deep behind enemy lines. Reach the other side. Take on big bad bugs. Then run for evac!


[h2] Buildcrafting: Classes [/h2] 
Every class has a primary, secondary, grenade slot, up to 2 utility slots, and up to 3 perk slots. These "up to's" are not class specific restrictions, but slots you globally unlock after hitting certain career ranks. Weapons have up to 4 attachment slots- optics, magazine, internal (like barrels), ammo type.

Guardian: Take aggro, Tank damage, lock down ore drills. Deployable shield circle. Call squadmates into the circle when things get busy. Bash enemies back when you activate shield. Ignore knockback with shield to secure scuffed revives.

Demolisher: Blow stuff up, even yourself! Destroy bug holes. Nuke bug hives. Hold choke points. Cleanup Corpses. Shoot a cannon from your back. 

Sniper: Jetpack up high. Spot enemies first with VISR and scanner gun. Take down gunner bugs and big single targets.

Ranger: Kite and mark enemies. Take materials back to base. Place rally points for the whole team. Grab stims and fly in for risky revives.

Engineer: Team ammo supply. Build and repair faster. Make resource drill objectives faster. Active ability lets you build and repair anywhere, anytime. Only class that can build spotlights.

Medic: Revive from a distance with the active ability. Supply everyone with forms of healing. Heal gun, heal vendor, heal beacon. Trade first-aid for buffs with combat stimulants or offense with a guard drone. passive health regen nearby medics?


[h2] Metaprogression: Armory Unlock system, Prestige [/h2] 
Armory: Break free of class restrictions. When you level 10 a weapon, any class can use it. Demo with a flamethrower? Sure! Engineer with autoshotgun? Go ahead!

Prestige: Unlock a new loadout slot and various cosmetics. Class progression is reset but Career Rank unlocks are preserved (slots, cosmetics) and Weapon Progression is preserved. (attachments, camos) You just have to re-earn the base gear back (Weapons, Utilities, Class Perks)


[h2] Misc things I like [/h2] 
It runs great on linux, give it a look on ProtonDB.

Various objectives will have caches next to them. Once opened, they will contain any random weapon or utility from any class, AND ANY CLASS CAN TAKE THEM. IN ANY SLOT! AND YOU GET XP FOR USING THAT WEAPON EVEN IF IT ISN'T UNLOCKED! These little boxes are so much fun, you never know what's inside or maybe you just want to use another gun to shake things up.

There's two +1 util perks, which CAN BE STACKED, and even give +10 shots for stim gun and scanner gun utilities! EACH! I was ready to start a mission and say "meh I guess I have 12 stim shots now instead of 10" nope I have 30!! it's great!! these also up my stim stacks from 3 per stack to 4, or 5! and soon we will have a perk that starts us with 6 stims, will I get to reach 8 stims a stack with that new perk? we'll just have to find out!


[h2] Problems with the game [/h2]
The maps can be really confusing. SPARTA and Boreas especially.

Progression can be buggy sometimes, like I completed 3 missions that all told me I hit level 70 but only after the third mission did I properly rank up from level 69.

There is a nuke launcher in the game and with the right setup it can be spammed to the point of absurdity. You won't be able to shoot anything because your screen will be shaking so much.

Explosives in this game give off wet fart vibes. They practically have to be on top of enemies if not direct hits to deal good damage, and the VFX of these explosions leave a lot to be desired.

Customization menu is broken, the visors look worse here than they do in-mission. Olive visor straight up doesn't work correctly in this menu.

Server connection can really make-or-break the joy you get out of the game. When it's laggy, everyone suffers. Shoot early and this is mostly mitigated, but where it gets especially bad is when you are trying to mantle up something or climb ladders and it just warps you back down because it's struggling so much to keep up.

The UX for picking a spawn point feels too barebones and lacking in information, Ranger's rally beacons are the only reason I know this is a feature in the game. Critical Strike missions and Hive Hunts on the SPARTA really suffer for this where players who aren't in the know will just be single file line meat in the grinder until the mission fails for running out of respawns.

The game could use a ballbuster difficulty to really test the limits of 16 players.

[h3]What will you find here?[/h3]
[b]Group vs Horde PvE shooter gameplay.[/b] It is a bit more dynamic and casual than ArmA encounters, but slower and more realistic than Serious Sam.
[b]Variability of missions and difficulties.[/b] From "build a base and stand a waves of enemies" to "run through the caves and demolish the enemy base". Randomized encounters, mission pathways and mutators (enemy and map perks) can turn a familiar mission to a deadly challenge.
[b]Tactical building elements.[/b] Most of the mission types require base building and focused on build'n'protect. Your success highly depends on what your team build and which formation they keep.
[b]Class based abilities.[/b] You choose 1 of 6 battle professions each session and play this role till the session ends. This role determines your percs and weapons. If you're disappointed with your choice, use a stationary machine gun.
[b]Group oriented gameplay.[/b] Supporting the group and laying on group support is how you win the mission. So resurrect them, heal them, support'em with fire and keep together to be supported. Ignoring your mates or playing solo Rambo is a way to loose the battle.

[h3]What won't you find here?[/h3]
[b]No any kind of PvP.[/b] PvE only. We are troopers, they are bugs. You can't play as a bug. You can't be an enemy trooper. Any type of intentional harm to your group mate is taken as trolling and greefing.

[b]Personal skill[/b] is not really necessary. Well, some skilled tricks may be useful, but focusing fire, knowing action priorities and situational awareness have won way more battles here. You can win the veteran mode with mediocre shooters, if they know where to shoot.
[b]Nuclear weapon?[/b] Yes, you can use it in this game. Sometimes you regret it.

I love this game. The team dynamic is fun, there are very few "go it alone" play options, especially on harder difficulties, so you really need to coordinate with other players. It's decently challenging, even for veteran crews. The game is innovative with its carnage system (bug corpses don't despawn but become part of the landscape and bugs can use them as ramps to get to you, like the movie). The play style is fun with classes that have cool features and perks that help them stand out.

The major limitation is performance. I have a decent system and still get periodic rubber banding and lag ... so I opt to play classes with splash damage so it matters a bit less. If you play the smaller map modes it seems to be better. The performance will improve over time, every update is mostly optimizations at this point, and it has improved significantly since the 1.0 launch. But there's nothing more infuriating than thinking you're out of a horde just to lag and snap back to the middle of it :D

Overall I have no complaints about this game other than performance, and that's improving steadily with each update.

Having put over 150 hours into this game at the time of writing, I can confidently say that it has held my attention far better than other coop horde shooters in recent years. I keep coming back to ST:E long after having lost interest in Helldivers 2 and Space Marine 2. The only games in it's genre that I have put more time into are World War Z and Aliens Fireteam, both games I have had far longer. ST:E feels very similar to the latter 2 games of that comparison and I can fully recommend it to anyone who enjoyed either of those equally excellent games.

The game consists of a very basic gameplay loop for the most part, building a base and defending it from waves of bugs, or defending an objective under similar circumstances. Its an extremely fun and addicting gameplay system that doesn't get boring even after hundreds of hours! The class system has, over time, become much more expansive. This means they now all feel a lot more unique and contribute to a more dynamic gameplay feel when cooperating with other players. The game also has an incredible soundtrack that perfectly invokes the feeling of the original Poledouris score while maintaining its own identity.

The games biggest flaw is its performance. The game launched in early access in 2023 and still suffers from significant slow down, frame drops, and pop in even on high end rigs. Connection issues are abundant too and often seem entirely random and can result in being kicked from matches. Something that is a huge inconvenience when matches often take over 30 minutes. There are also a list of bugs that can occur from time to time and you will likely come across at least one in every match you play.

The game is one of the most fun shooters I have played in years and it is on that basis that I can recommend the game wholeheartedly. However, those without a tolerance for the performance issues and bugs would be more than justified in avoiding this title, especially as it  has now officially released for full price. A move which is very disappointing given its current state. I would urge anyone that is interested in the game, but hesitant about buying it, to check back regularly as the game continues to be patched.

This will be a fairly honest and direct review.

The game is very good in concept and very poor in execution.  I have a pretty heavy machine and I get constant FPS drops for no apparent reason while my machine is not even at 25% load on processor, RAM, and graphics card.  And when I say FPS drops, I mean like 5 FPS and my inputs don't work at all.  Like, I can move with WASD, but no matter how often I push fire, I don't fire.  If I pull out my grenade, I keep it in my hand and don't throw it.  It's like any kind of fire button is disabled during frame stuttering.  Like, Valve should probably pull this off Steam until the devs actually make the game playable.  At this point, it is probably stealing and could feasibly be argued in court.

I picked up this game in early access and it was really solid.  It was an easy "shut your brain off" PvE game and those roots are still secure in foundation.  You get standard classes with a role that nobody actually uses the class for at all (medics not reviving, assaulters staying on defense, engineers not doing any engineering at all).  Somehow you can still usually win on normal this way, but you can still lose as well.

The weapons need heavy revisions because they don't do their intended job well, but it's still a bit charming with how unbalanced it is (and not in your favor).  The classes all have their own unique skills, perks, and equipment.  The Demolisher, for instance, can become a suicide bomber with a fully automatic shotgun and a melee attack that shatters dead bugs, and an arm one of those football people would envy.  The engineer can build stuff like turrets outside of base.  The assaulter can get a little boost towards the opponent and lay new spawn points for the team.  That kind of stuff.

Every time they release an update, the game gets worse.  Not in concept, but technically.  More bugs are introduced, others aren't fixed, the optimization gets worse (somehow).  Nobody seems to have an answer as to why and the development team seemingly has chosen to just not acknowledge the problem, let alone fix it.  Been a while since I could even complete a single mission.

Speaking of this.  The game crashes all the time.  I realize this is a problem with UE5 in general, but I can't make it through missions anymore it seems.  Crash to desktop and once it caused an entire BSOD on crash.  And in the rare case your game doesn't crash, the server you're playing on does.  

There are other flaws with game play, but most of those are what I would consider part of the game's charm.  Like occasionally just running hundreds more at you than it should even though your map has no mutations or anything.  Or accidentally spawning in like 10 tigers at once for you to mow down.  Or overwhelming you so much you can't leave the starting area.

But the technical "achievements" of this game seem more like proof of concept than even a beta, let alone official release.  If you buy this I would consider setting an alarm at one and a half hours before considering to refund it.  I really hope they fix it because it has immense potential and console players don't seem to have nearly as many issues.  But right now, for PC, I would genuinely consider skipping this one until optimization issues have been fixed.  But I could easily see them abandoning PC all together and only focusing on console with how much console players seem to like it.

난 호드 모드를 하고 싶은데 호드 모드가 아예 안뜰때도 있음.

3. 무기
각 클래스 별로 특화된 무기가 1~2개씩 있음
이 무기를 만렙 찍으면 무기고 시스템이 발동되는데

특정 클래스 레벨이 되어야 됨.
즉, 스나 중 가장 대미지 높은 스나가 Morita XXX 라는 바렛 닮은 스나총이 있는데
13렙인가 부터 사용가능함. 무기고 마크가 붙어도 클래스 레벨이 13렙 되지 않으면 못쓰는데
이 전까진 그냥 기본 무기만 써야됨.
세계관 특성상 무기가 별로 없어서 이해는 한다만... 좀 더 추가됐으면 하는 바람?

이 게임이 아시아 서버가 있지만 오후엔 평균 3~5분 기다려야 잡히는 경우가 있고

The game brilliantly channels the iconic dialogue from the movie, where every line is a rallying cry for survival. Killing bugs isn’t just an action—it’s a noble mission to save mankind!

Every time you fire your weapon, you’re not just eliminating pesky alien pests; you’re taking a stand for humanity. The gameplay is infused with the spirit of the movie, where each explosive encounter echoes the familiar banter and bravado that made the original such a cult classic. And in the midst of the chaos, when the bug swarms are at their fiercest, you shout out with pride, "I'm doing my part!"—a personal declaration that fuels the fight.

This isn’t just about mindless shooting; it’s about rallying together and making a difference. So, trooper, suit up, do your part for mankind, and get out there to show those bugs who’s boss. With its perfect mix of humor, heart, and high-stakes action, Starship Troopers: Extermination is the ultimate call to arms for anyone ready to join the frontlines and save the world—one bug at a time!

"Starship Troopers: Extermination" is a triumphant love letter to the 1997 cult-classic film, delivering an adrenaline-pumping, bug-blasting experience that captures the chaotic spirit of the Mobile Infantry’s war against the Arachnids. As a 16-player co-op FPS, it throws you into sprawling battlefields where teamwork is your only hope against relentless waves of alien insects. The game shines in its ability to evoke the movie’s over-the-top action, with every match feeling like a desperate stand-off—whether you’re unloading clips into a swarm of Warriors or watching a Tiger bug tear through your defenses. The visceral thrill of seeing hundreds of bugs spill across the horizon, paired with the satisfying crunch of their demise under your Morita rifle, makes every victory feel hard-earned and exhilarating.

What sets "Extermination" apart is its innovative base-building mechanic, seamlessly blending tower defense with shooter chaos. You and your squad aren’t just surviving—you’re constructing walls, turrets, and bunkers to stem the tide, turning each mission into a frantic exercise in coordination and strategy. The persistence of bug corpses adds a brilliant twist, transforming the battlefield into a grotesque obstacle course as their bodies pile up, creating ramps for their brethren to scale your fortifications. It’s a small detail that amplifies the sense of scale and desperation, making every firefight visually spectacular and tactically dynamic. Add in six distinct classes—each with unlockable weapons and perks—and you’ve got a game that rewards both individual skill and collective effort.

Sure, it’s not without its rough edges—occasional jank and a lackluster single-player mode might irk some—but these fade against the sheer fun of its multiplayer core. "Starship Troopers: Extermination" nails the franchise’s gritty, gung-ho vibe, from the propaganda-laden loading screens to Casper Van Dien’s grizzled Johnny Rico barking orders. It’s a game that doesn’t overthink itself, embracing its B-movie roots with unapologetic gusto. For fans of the film or anyone craving a co-op shooter with personality and scale, this is a must-play—a stellar romp that proves the only good bug is a dead one, and there’s no shortage of them here.

Starship Troopers: Extermination is an OKAY game at best and is the poor man's Helldivers 2. Right off the bat you notice a big problem when you join a random match. There are 15 other random people and at least 13 people have no idea what they are doing. Most missions have objectives that aren't killing bugs and unfortunately killing bugs is the only thing those 13 other players do. So missions take twice as long as they should or the mission fails because you get overrun. Imagine Helldivers 2 chaos, but with even more DUMBA** players. 

The game is also very buggy, expect to get stuck on things. Expect the bugs to have bugs, it's really interesting watching the enemy bugs stand around like they are lost on what to do. It's even more interesting to watch the bugs glitch through walls and buildings. This doesn't look good, and it doesn't seem to be a high priority for the devs to get it fixed. I've read a lot of people complain about how the game runs on their machines, I noticed lag for a moment maybe once in 4 matches but overall optimization didn't seem like it was a problem for me. 

Also there are solo missions that teach you the various mission types as well as show you the ins and outs of the bug killing community. However, the problem with that is, the AI in your squad are piss poor teammates. It makes the solo missions so awful that you'll just want to skip them and most probably do. Which also explains why random players in your matches have no idea what to do but point and shoot bugs.  

One positive if you like this kind of thing, ST:E is quite a bit more chaotic than Helldivers 2, only because I think there's more going on. You have the ability to build in this game in certain parts of missions. Mostly you are building defenses but that can get quite crazy with 16 people building wildly. You'll then be tasked with protecting your base by killing bugs and repairing defenses. It'll be nonstop explosions. You'll have smoke, fire and bug guts all messing with your vision to make it even more insane. Overall the experience is very intense in those parts of each mission.

My thoughts for an overall grade on my review is a positive IF you are are getting it on sale. I don't believe it is worth $29.99 USD in it's current state. If you don't have friends to play with, you probably won't enjoy playing with randoms. You'll likely be stuck doing the boring parts of the mission if you even want a chance to pass the mission. It has too many glitches and things that simply aren't getting fixed. I don't believe the the developers (Offworld) truly are going to take the time to improve the game in the ways it needs it most. I suggest 9 times out of 10, you should pass on ST:E and go play or buy Helldivers 2 instead.

[h1]From A First Glance[/h1]

Sep 2024: Will change review in near future if/when worthy improvements for our money is made.

[h2]How is this game fun?[/h2]
The fun part is shooting bugs. Tons of them. Graveyards worth of bugs. You're invading a planet of bugs that presumably did nothing to you and you are encouraged to commit genocide on these bugs [b][u][i]AND[/i][/u][/b] that's about it... for now. As you may suspect, it's a game where they replace humans as bugs and incite you to commit genocide (I recommend you dig deeper to finding out what actual country on Earth guarantees citizenship for your military service whilst committing alleged genocide on a people whom are called animals/bugs/dehumanised, the answer lies in the lobby on the top left the logo above the word "Vanguard").

You satisfy your craving of emptying hundreds of rounds into these 1's and 0's and you'll look at your Steam library what other investments you had made to fulfil other cravings.

[h2]The game relies on uninteresting objectives[/h2]
A lot of players hang around base and neglect objectives. [i][u]If the objectives were fun, everyone would run to do them[/u][/i] but these objectives don't carry any real meaning of what contributes to a victory or its opposite. When the match ends with a "victory" or "defeat" we feel completely [b]indifferent[/b] about it.

You're not met with an interesting boss to fight with different mechanics/strategies to explore. This is simply a sandbox physics of guns that can shoot at bugs with simple list of objectives whether you complete them or not.

[h2]It's EARLY ACCESS silly[/h2]
Early access is supposed to give us a taste of what to expect down the road and encourage others to invest. What am I investing in? A game like any other? There are other games that allow me to shoot bugs, this offers less and asks for more money.

[h2]My Steam Friends[/h2]
The highest hours played among my Steam friends is roughly 4 hours.

[h2]Game Performance for a Budget PC[/h2]
Considering it's from the makers of Squad I was a little concerned that my budget PC would perform poorly but to my surprise it seems better optimized than most early access games I've come across. With an RX6600 and Ryzen 5 5500 I'm rocking anywhere between 60FPS (intense combat) to 120FPS (idle) on Low graphics with Ultra Performance for FSR (great job adding FSR devs).

Despite low graphical settings the game looks great enough to be immersed.

[h2]Do I Regret The Purchase?[/h2]
Yes, it's 40$ just to satisfy a minor craving that hasn't come back...

[h2]If the Starship Troopers movie was a poem, this game would be a gonzo porn where the lead actress only figures out it's porn when someone's already clapping her cheeks.[/h2]

[b]Grinding for Tools, Not Fun.[/b]
When the progression is just a bar getting filled with a few unlocks behind, the best you could unlock here is yet another gun and all of these, from my understanding, need to be unlocked repeatedly. You might want to use the gun B over the one in class A but you're forced to level that other class first. Does the in-game system need to be different? Not really. These systems, where you unlock content by reaching certain levels, have worked well in dozens of other games. The problem is that these tools you unlock have to have some sort of fun behind them, and unfortunately in this game, they don't get far from being just tools; they're pretty much just an Excel tabs hitting the screen.

[b]Dead in the water character customization.[/b]
Everybody looks the same, and what little you can change is so small it wouldn't make a difference had there been no customization at all. I’m not asking for clown skins, but a few options to make your look different or maybe unique. Also, giving players a sense of progression via visual build-up? That's something this game does not do at all. And it gets even better when half of the already mediocre content is locked behind a paywall. Is this a F2P game with a purchase fee, or am I missing something?

[b]Over the top effects killing the bleak visual aspect of the original.[/b]
Bright happy colour schemes, glowing claws for bugs - what else is there to say? Fortnite kids must be happy. At places, there's so much VFX going on you're getting lost in explosions and tons of shiny effects. Have the people behind the game ever played it themselves? Is this the intended player experience? Lots of other games with huge player filled lobbies manage to keep chaotic action on screen without turning it into a visual mess where you can't tell what’s going on.

[b]Mechanics that are half-made.[/b]
There's a cool feature where bug bodies pile up on each other, and it looks fantastic yet you can’t even destroy them with your grenades? Bugs die instantly from these, but somehow body piles get x100 armor?

[b]Bugs are not scary or threatening: all their character is lost.[/b]
The movie's tone was grim, full of blood and terror. This game does none of that. Even the RTS set in the same universe had more charm. This just feels like another soulless project to suck money out of the IP. And these are the people who made Squad? A game that was well-received and praised? They better start looking for a new meaning in life if this is the best they can do one of the most boring game designs I’ve played in years.

And the bugs, they don’t even climb the fu3k1ng walls. You can stay there all day long. The only thing that'll hit you is the machine gun bug. Oh yes, you made him OP so people wouldn't camp there. In my two-hour experience (maybe I just missed it), I didn't see a single flying bug. Not one! And when the bugs do attack, they do it in the most lame way - through holes in the walls or by walking on piles of their dead bodies (which only happened during the 10th wave on mid difficulty). They don't surround you in numbers, they just spawn in and run back. There's no immersion in this game at all. It gives you the vibe of a school project made by five guys solely because they had nothing else to do that summer. And unfortunately, in a bad way.

[b]When the composer was told to do his job just to fulfill a contract.[/b]
There's a great main theme, it really captures something beautiful and has a unique 90s vibe. I genuinely love it. Yet every other track in the game, especially the battle theme which in the movie hyped you up so much you weren't sitting in your chair anymore, you were fighting bugs is so shallow. Even boosting the sound from 50% (default) to 75% doesn’t help. It feels like a track poorly handled by AI: a bunch of parts stitched together that make no sense. They're not grand, they don't hype you, your heart doesn't pump; it's just as mediocre as mediocrity gets.

[b]Creature and world design.[/b]
One of the rare things this game does right is weapon design: they look absolutely abnormal compared to real-life firearms, and that's what makes them so special. They also carry the vibe of the movie. The walls and human-made tech also look solid, especially when the lighting hits them just right. Without proper lighting, though, the game gives off PS3-era visuals, with lots of modern features missing. It hits the bugs the most they look overly cartoony, losing anything remotely terrifying. And that's not just because of visuals, it's also on how the game plays and treats these creatures.

[b]Little detail which could be missed.[/b]
Voice messages auto-translated in chat are a great feature. I really like it, as I feel weird talking to complete strangers with no face using voice chat.

[b]20 Hz servers.[/b]
Do we live in the 90s? I get that equipment isn't cheap, but you're the ones selling skins. Costs are up, right?

[b]Get in and out in minutes.[/b]
10 GB file size, fast to download and fast to uninstall.

[b]Predatory EULA. Read it for yourself.[/b]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3539461012
[b]Is it actually fun? Can it be fun?[/b]
The only remote sense of fun I had was on wave 10. The 9 waves before that were filled with boredom. You can't change your class once you deploy if you don't like your chosen playstyle, you're stuck with it for the entire match. The map I played had everyone standing in one zone, fending off waves of bugs. That, to me, wasn't fun. The shooting, visuals, gun sounds, and music weren't immersive or engaging.

I've played a lot of games with similar setups whether it's COD Zombies or Deep Rock Galactic and I have to say, this one does it the worst. It doesn't innovate, nor does it polish what's already been done better by other games. It's just a shallow product trying to capitalize on an existing franchise, one that's probably cheap to license.

This could be fun if it were the first game you ever played. But as it is, it's a 4.5/10 at best - a painfully dull experience that brings nothing to the genre except another capitalist-made, uninspired slop product.

[b]What It All Comes Down To.[/b]
This might be the worst game I've played in years. It feels like the kind of experience where you've got to be the one paid to play it, and now, looking at my friend list, I understand why none of them got a one on their account: you don't want that 3h1tst3in to get there just for you to clean it off.

There's no gameplay loop, no vision, and no soul. just wave after wave of missed opportunities. It does not respect the movie, nor probably the book the movie was based off. And sad as it is to say, this game somehow makes Killing Floor 3 look good. If that's not enough for you to make off it, then what the hell are you doing here reading this?

Game released incredibly unfinished. Nothing that was excused as part of early access has been fixed in over a year. Online connection is jittery and janky. The actual gameplay is incredibly simple. Optimization is terrible. I'm on a top end PC and it still jitters and stutters when combat gets too busy - not because of FPS issues, but because the game itself just can't handle more than a couple dozen enemies. Persistent corpse update only made this worse.

Difficulty is a matter of how many times you can be revived. The game is full of one shots with enemies you can't avoid hitting you. Dying is essentially only a stun, though. Revive timers are comically long and medics have a 0 risk rez drone they can toss at you from a mile away. So the difficulty is centered around being knocked over like bowling pins just to be set back up in a moment. No enemy has anything else to it. There's a couple bugs that shoot you from range but overall it's just bug, bigger HP sack bug, biggest sponge bug.

The UI is barebones and barely functional. Items unequip from loadouts. Weapons get randomly autoequipped and there's no way to customize your loadout once you're in a match, so if you load in and mouse over your class, if it suddenly has the wrong weapon uh, screw you I guess.

The clan system is a single page with a list of randomly chosen clans. You can't join your friends because there's no way to invite people and the only way to find a clans is to look at the randomly chosen list of 20ish public offerings. There's no search, no "next page" buttons, etc.

I honestly regret supporting this game. Play Helldivers instead.

Extermination is a spin off game from cult movie about Starship Troopers, which carries a lot of heavy lifting for the lore. If you are fresh off watching that movie, sorry to say, this game is not connected to it in any way. You get the model of Arachnids and janky movement (Frame Generation on UE5 engine is supposed to fix that by design of developers) and that movement isnt frame dropping, its simply bad animations. You also get a good model of guns they use in movie, and maybe sound? If you wanted to coop with your buddies and meme to oblivion, sorry, this game is not for you. Its a generic shooter with horde enemies. Now, how can you screw that up? Well, ask developers. They had this game in early access for years now, and it is still unfinished. 

Performance: It is classic UE5 product. It depends on modern card features and it gives nothing to justify that. Textures are meh, animation is meh, particles and backgrounds are meh, worlds are meh. I mean, how hard would it be to go through the movie and recreate the backdrops and invent some new? Imagine if you also cared enough to look through comic books and take some of that? Yeah, Offworld doesnt do that. There is frame drops, there is poor performance, but there is also janky animations that may look like frame drops, but it is just a byproduct of unfinished game.

Sound: There is no voice commands. Easy solution would be to have a voice command system like in Smite for example, that you can memorise with 3 letter shortcuts and give your team quick instructions that would be movie lore accurate. Well, apparently that is too much work. And for game that is full price they couldnt be bothered to licence movie soundtrack for this nor create some new theme based music. Music in game is uninspiring at best.

Design: Hope you like rocks.

Gameplay: If you though this review had been overly negative, then I suggest you skip this part, because oh boy, I'm gonna be spitting some criticism (facts) here. Its a horde simulator, and a pretty bad one at that. Remember Space Marine? Well this game isnt close to that. With limited movement and slow progression, your skill wont matter, you will be forced to move at slow pace and grind. Base building is nice feature that is totally busted, as people dont have enough time to build or repair between waves. Builder menu is simple and cluttered at same time, probably because design artists were never considered in Offworld. Classes are a joke, and beside medic and engineer, you are pretty much just a grunt. So let me give you a positive example, battlefield 5. Imagine if this game was built by that team, and you had multiple options to approach the battlefield. It could still be a ticket shooter, but now you would have team that flies spaceships and fights in air, or extracts team in transports, and tanks and exoskeletons (again, look at comics). Imagine how much fun you could have with extractions, and bombardment, and recon and air battles, hell even story based coop hack and slash. Imagine voice chat being active and not broken (oh yeah, it is, it cuts out for everyone bit further away), or for people that dont wanna use it to go with voice commands? And from all the bugs, you get Arachnids, not even the flying ones. Where are the Tankers, the flying ones, the brain bugs? So one last point, all the weapons feel nerfed, like it take a lot of bullets to kill anything and its not even accuracy based. There are no headshots. Imagine if they gave us something futuristic, like a railgun, powersword, or any cannon or flamethrower? Or god forbid we had option to use toxic bombs.

These are all questions and suggestions for different dev team, because clearly Offworld doesnt care nor has the capacity to create something decent. A game with plenty of potential for fun, I mean, it's STARSHIP TROOPERS.
The game did an amazing job capturing all the humour and bloody zaniness of the movies, it has base-building, objectives that are (usually) relatively easy to achieve, and so much of it is fulfilling and viscerally pleasing, very immersive.

There's only a couple of problems that keep me from recommending this game:
1. Troll Players. In almost every match I played after the first couple of months, many of the people building bases actively work to make it impossible to defend or otherwise make the mission significantly more difficult. I spend almost as much time disassembling problematic structure placement so I can actually make a defensible position as I do shooting bugs.

2. Weapon Progression. At least as of the last time I played it, pretty much every weapon except the basic starter assault rifle and the heavy gun of the tank-class felt worthless. Using a sniper rifle was almost completely ineffective because it takes longer to kill the same warrior/worker bugs with the sniper than it does with the Mk. 1 rifle, for example. 

3. A Toxic Community. Again, perhaps it's evened out and changed, but I doubt it. In line with Troll Players, if you complain or comment about pretty much literally anything that could easily be resolved with a simple tweak or a buff to equipment in the forums, you're more likely to find yourself buried under various versions of "Get Good, lol noob" than receive any actual  vindication that your idea might have merit.

4. Sudden Extreme Difficulty. Because of the Randomly Generated Nature of the mission maps and objectives, there have been multiple occasions where a completion of the mission has been actively impossible, especially with the extraction phases. Having to run through a slavering and unending horde of bugs across the entire map, for example, sometimes with less time to do so than it actually takes to physically make that journey.

All in all, it's a wonderful game, but at least for me I don't see any reason to keep playing it. Grab a full server's worth of friends and have a blast, great for community game nights, etc, but as a predominantly solo player it's a toxic and unpleasant experience.

To address the obvious and most frequently asked question: no this game is not trying to be an alternative to Hell Divers 2 (HD2), nor vice versa.  While there are some similarities in enemy types and sci-fi setting, Starship Troopers: Extermination (SST:E) is a game with a very different gameplay and overall experience.  HD2 is a casual sci-fi shooter where the coop and squad loadouts are open-ended: players can choose to pick synergistic kits and work together cooperatively, but they can also zoom off to objectives on their own and remain viable (assuming the player is experienced and armed with the right equipment).  SST:E by comparison is a much more hardcore coop shooter, where players pick one of several defined roles and the teamplay and coordination is required in order to complete the mission.  It is very, very easy for the mission to be failed in this game if teams dont cooperate; quite often the mission will fail even if the teams do cooperate.  This game puts a huge emphasis on teamwork and the gameplay and player fun factor can truly suffer if that teamwork is lacking.

The game modes, player classes and emphasis on teamwork make this a unique and interesting the game.  However, I would not recommend buying this game in its current state.  The game is unstable and poorly optimized - i've had several crashes in the 8 or so hours at the time of this review and I see massive FPS drops when the bug attacks reach full force.  The matchmaking is absolutely horrible - there is no server list for players to browse through, rather they rely on matchmaking that randomly places the player with other randoms.  Players can use friend groups (for Steam, Xbox, PS) to join up with other players, but the process is way more complicated than it ought to be.  With the exception of some building tutorials, there is no real tutorial system to teach new players about the different game modes or class types. 
 There are other random glitches the player will encounter throughout - weapons loadouts constantly resetting for classes, getting stuck on dead bugs or terrain.

This game has potential, but it needs a lot of work and refinement in order to be considered truly playable.  Im not sure if OWI has the patience or the financial inclination to put the necessary work into this game.  I'd advise new players to wait and see.

I have over 30 hours in-game now and have encountered a few game-breaking glitches. Often, after dying, you will glitch out and be unable to shoot or turn your head. The only workaround is to pause, redeploy, or be killed. When switching between weapons, the sights sometimes glitch and display the perspective of the previous weapon, making aiming difficult. Occasionally, after reloading and switching between a special ability, the gun will not be reloaded when you attempt to shoot, leaving you scrambling to load a new magazine while bugs swarm your face. I've also respawned into a glitch where you're endlessly falling through the map and dying because the spawn area is cluttered with walls built by the team. This drained my team's tickets—about seven times less—until the game finally managed to spawn me in. Many of the weapons, including the primary assault rifle, feel underpowered, so each kill of a "standard bug" isn't very satisfying. I've tried all the classes in the game, and most of their weapons and abilities also feel weak, almost like a gimmick, especially when you've seen the original movie and the devastation an AR can cause to a bug. It takes an entire magazine to kill a single bug, even with the auto-shotgun (unless you hit a weak spot), which makes the kill feel pretty lame. People have spoken online in reviews about how they need to change the way the Galactic War Mode or whatever its called works. By making it more of a turn based war claiming bug planets by way of battle. After a planet has been claimed you go to the next planet and the next until the campaign is completed. That would make the Horde mode make more sense if after a mission is failed the team is gathered to a point on the planet to defend like "the Alamo" until swept off planet by a dropship. Then the team is regathered, you go back to the same planet, and fight again to claim it, planet by planet until the war is finally done. I really feel like the game could use dismemberment similar to the movies. Bug arms and legs getting physically shot off by your gain fire depending on the body part you target, then the bugs movement could be slowed down. Also, the marines could once in a while be picked up by certain stronger bugs, and torn apart limb by limb. I feel it would feel more like the movies if it was so. Casper Van Dien or "Rico" could also be used to narrate the Galactic war missions, and dont lock players out if they're in a clan or not. There's much work to be done here, but I have faith that they can make it great. There's so much untapped potential in this game.
