In the current state of the game it is not worth your investment.  The game holds promise of what could be but failure by the devs to properly curate their game and improve it has led to a state where there are many obscure mechanics that make no sense.

Issues I find present with the game current


- The common warrior bug which can spawn an endless swarms can one hit kill you if you are not the guardian class during its charge attack, two hit kill otherwise and send you flying with a single hit.

- Bombardment effects
                 1: Bombardments from plasma bugs come from straight above you and have zero hint as to where they are landing unless you look straight up.  This means you are not looking in front of you and die to the one hit/two hit kill warrior bugs.
                 2: Explosive pill bugs can spawn anywhere and launch themselves at your constructions as an engineer (and note, they only launch themselves at your constructions or medic stim machines, no one else), make a noise that sounds like mortars falling from the sky and are barely the size of a basketball on the ground.  They are hard to react to and even if you do shoot them to try and save your buildings it blows up the bug anyways blowing up your structures.  A single pill bug is enough to kill you and instantly destroy your engineering structures.  It even can fall out of the cave roofs on maps with such.
                  3:  Inferno bug bomardments kill you before you can even stim yourself given the delay on the stim.  They kill faster than you can react to it.

- Engineer bugs and mechanics
                   1:  You get to make 1000 resource worth of buildings that also have a limited count, including only 1 turret and 1 turret ammo dump.  That is fine on paper but if for some reason you are unable to make it back to the buildings you made, they are there for good and counting against your maximum building cap for the rest of the mission crippling your CLASS ABILITY.  So then you cannot make another ammo dump or turret for example if you have one elsewhere on the map.
                    2:  Engineering placement for their personal building is very finicky with only being able to be placed on extremely level surfaces that half the time ends up far enough away from the objective that its useless or the only place you can place the stuff down is where the bugs spawn from surrounding the objective.  Good luck manning a turret when a tiger and multiple warriors spawn on top of you.
                    3:  The engineering flamethrower blinds you and team mates turning your entire screen black.  In some cases its been reported that it makes their entire screen black for the rest of the game and it has caused headaches due to the visual effects.

- Extraction from the base at the end of the mission sucks for anyone but mobility classes as they commonly leave everyone behind to extract alone.  It leaves a sour taste at the end of your gameplay when you die constantly unable to extract alive and meanwhile that sniper which spent the entire mission up on a tower someplace in no danger is on the ship alive.

My biggest complaint however would be the community on discord including its moderators hired by the Staff.  They are some of the most close minded people when it comes to quality of life features, changes, or anything that would help improve a new players experience.  

I brought up concerns some friends of mine had with trying to get into this game and my response from them was along the lines of "Skill issue, get better, join a large group and only play with them" among other reasons as to why they should gatekeep the game from new players.  Like why have a quickplay feature if you can only properly enjoy the game in a large group?


In the end the its a game that holds great promise for a niche of large PvE coop gameplay but fails to meet the mark after being in early access for a year, failing to maintain a minimum of 1000 active players, and continue to fail to curate their toxic community which wants to keep the game in a state of an 'old boys club' where only they can enjoy it.

+ Much better performance
+ More enemy variety and objectives
+ Solid weapon feel and handling
+ More classes

+/- Customization is lackluster
+/- No handcrafted, narrative-driven campaign

- Basic, empty environments with low detail (e.g. repetitive textures that are obvious when applied to large, flat surfaces, making maps look like they were created with tech 15 years ago, as well as limited atmospheric and environmental activity that would bring the environment to life)
- Basic SFX (e.g. bug explosions look unfinished; nuke explosions feel flat and underwhelming)
- Enemy movement can be incredibly spastic and hard to track, especially during CQC

Starship Troopers: Extermination offers a solid foundation for an co-op FPS PvE game, but is desperate need of more sophisticated asset design and environmental detail, particularly the type that would make the world feel alive, in order to reach its full potential.

I want to start by acknowledging that I understand that this game is multiplayer focused first and foremost.
What initially brought me to purchase Early access was early development promise that they will add bots/singleplayer mode in future. later they posted in one of roadmaps that they thinking about adding singleplayer once game hit full release as they have bots working but they want to find more interesting ways they could use them. 
A few months before full release we have squad member (bot) bios & hype articles about who they are and what they do. Now we hit that long awaited full release 1.0. and what? We have singleplayer "campaign" which is half-baked tutorial for multiplayer mode which doesn't explain topics like base building (granted there is separate tutorial for that) or what are priority targets, difference between bugs, weapons, how to utilize classes to fullest potential, how to use different classes for advanced tactics. no, its set of simple on paper 25 missions that are sometimes hard due to brain-dead bots (they remind me of colonial marine game AI team members). When they said they need to time thinking how to implement them in more interesting and fun ways, i was really hoping that singleplayer mode will be something similar idea of how matches are setup in multiplayer, difference would be that you are platoon commander and can issue orders to squad leaders to defend base or advance to side objectives while you tackle more important objectives with your squad. i guess more interesting way for devs was buggy & half unresponsive bots that follow you around like ducklings. i don't understand why they hyped your team members with articles if for the most part they are nameless mooks that follow you around. can i play this tutorial to grind weapon & other unlockables? no. but i guess this IS multiplayer game after all.  Another issue i have with post full release is that there is unlockables & missions that are locked behind company system. i wont get into detail as there is big outcry regarding that system already, but for me as mostly solo player, it means that there is content i will never be able see or have, yet i paid full price for game. 
Granted, multiplayer mode IS fun. game is set around idea that Federation is on offence or trying to hold line/mount counter attack after Bugs offence, and game feels like it, you and usually 15 other grunts push forward or stand ground against unending wave of bugs (Klendathu & programming kind). match usually is around 25-35 mins if you have guys on team that know map layout & know what they are doing once you have those few precious minutes to build up your base defenses. If you are unlucky, match can get more then hour, and you will be disconnected from game or forced to quit match because Bugs bug out & match cant end properly (so no xp for all that spent time).
Overall I'd would surmise my current feeling regarding game as broken promise.  Yeah i knows it is MP focused game. Up to 16 players. But if you say several times that there will be bots, there will be singleplayer mode, you have more interesting ideas regarding how to use them as game can have up to 16 grunts, you even bother to hype up those bots, and you dropdown half baked tutorial super generic "campaign" with barely functional bots, i feel really cheated. it is really disappointing as I think this game had & still has real potential to be fun, might i even say, THE BEST FPS/RTR hybrid game out there, and there aren't a lot of those last i checked. 
But man, last time i was so let down by gaming hype was DoW3. I will probably play this from time to time as like i said, MP aspect of game IS fun. But failure to keep promises regarding SP aspect of game really soured me on recommending it to anyone.

[b]Starship Troopers: Extermination[/b] - great potential buried under technical issues. When Starship Troopers: Extermination finally left Early Access, I expected the real “bugs” to be the ones we fight, not the ones in the optimization. Sadly, the game still struggles with performance, connectivity, and questionable system design choices that hold it back from being truly great.
[h3]What’s Good:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Fun co-op gameplay and large-scale battles.
[*]Cross-play sounds good on paper.
[*]Solid atmosphere that captures the Starship Troopers vibe.
[/list]
[h3]What’s Not So Good:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Optimization issues remain largely unchanged even after full release.
[*]Performance drops and stutters in active fights.
[*]Cross-play matchmaking is slow and unreliable.
[*]Random disconnects during loading - including being kicked with “squad is full” errors.
[*]Company (clan) system is overly restrictive: only 30 members, limited permissions.
[*]Regular members can’t start missions, making event participation nearly impossible for solo players.
[*]Players in less active time zones struggle even more due to fixed mission schedules.
[*]Time-limited events feel like a second job when you depend on someone else’s timing.
[*]Paid DLC offering only a few skins/icons.
[/list]
[b]Overall:[/b]
Starship Troopers: Extermination has the foundation of a great co-op shooter, but its technical issues and restrictive systems drag the game down at every step. After leaving Early Access, these problems are no longer excusable - especially when paired with questionable monetization decisions.
[b]My advice:[/b]
If you and your friends enjoy co-op shooters and can tolerate performance issues, you’ll still have fun.
But if you expect a polished experience after 1.0 - be prepared for disappointment.

One of the main criticisms of Starship Troopers: Extermination is its repetitive gameplay. The game revolves around killing waves of bugs, and there is not much variation in the enemies or environments. This can make the game feel repetitive and grindy after a while.

Another common complaint is the technical issues. The game has been reported to have performance problems, such as stuttering and frame drops. There have also been reports of bugs and glitches that can disrupt the gameplay experience.

Some players also find the lack of depth in Starship Troopers: Extermination to be disappointing. There is no real story to the game, and the characters are one-dimensional. The game also lacks any meaningful progression or customization options.

Despite these criticisms, Starship Troopers: Extermination has its fans. Many players enjoy the game for its fast-paced action and co-op gameplay. The game is also a good option for fans of the Starship Troopers franchise who are looking for a new way to experience the universe.

Overall, Starship Troopers: Extermination is a mixed bag. It has its strengths and weaknesses, and whether or not it is a good game for you will depend on your personal preferences. If you are looking for a fast-paced, action-packed co-op game with a nostalgic feel, then Starship Troopers: Extermination might be worth checking out. However, if you are looking for a deep and engaging game with a lot of replay value, then you might want to look elsewhere.

For example, movement is generally fine. The speed and responsiveness is all good, you feel like you have full control of your character. Or you may be enjoying the most frantic battle with countless arachnids surrounding you, and you are battling them to the last blood. Until you pull out the health stim to heal yourself and magically the stim does not work, resulting in your death that is unwarranted.

Or you could be retreating from the pursuit of the arachnids and the arachnids starts teleporting. Or you could be throwing a resource canister to your teammate and suddenly physics nope out of existence and the canister starts to move erratically away from you.

The game is a conglomerate of implemented systems that have good concepts and design, but lack any amount of polishing to make the systems work as intended. In software dev 80% of the work is polishing. But this game shipped out 20% of the effort and called it a day.

So the game has nice mechanics and systems, good visuals and designs. But terrible implementation and absurd amount of bugs. Is it fun? Yes. Is it worth on a good sale? Yes. Is it frequently frustrating to play? Yes.

I got this game in early access for $30. It was a great, if simple game early on. As the updates progressed and the launch of 1.0 drew near, things began to deteriorate rapidly. Updates began being a lot more buggy and having performance issues. The engine transition to UE5 made things a lot more unstable and messy overall. After 1.1 the game is in a pretty sorry state. Optimization and stability is horrible, the game crashes almost every every time I launch it, the bug animations are stiff and clunky, and I swear bugs have been double or triple hitting players per animation as you no longer have the ability to get surrounded and extricate yourself or have amazing final stands like before way back in early access. You get surrounded, you're dead instantly regardless of class and difficulty.

The single player campaign is not even a campaign. It's a glorified tutorial that is needlessly and painfully drawn out over 25 missions. Even then it fails to go into comprehensive base building mechanics outside of what key to use to bring out your build tool and to deconstruct or repair. It is boring, tedious, repetitive and uninteresting. It's just flat and hollow with nothing of real value outside of the most basic information that could be useful to a new player if they have the fortitude to go through every single mission in the few hours it would take. It is nice the campaign gives you weapon XP and is probably the only redeeming thing about it so you can turn off your brain and grind a low XP weapon or two.

Overall the game had promise and was quite fun in early access. Now it's a buggy, unoptimzed and disjointed mess. I would struggle to justify purchasing it for $30 in its current state, let alone the full asking price the game ascended to after the 1.0 launch. This game is in desperate need of being rebuilt or heavily passed with optimizations, fixes, and tweaks. Unless this game one day makes a big turn around and focuses on fixing itself give it a pass unless you get a hefty discount or sale. Your money is better spent elsewhere at the moment. Space Marine 2 and Helldivers 2 are much better alternative games if you need to scratch your horde shooter fix.

Rubber banding issues are constant, bug AI is strange and confused at times, I've been trapped in the respawn screen before and had to disconnect to escape it among other issues.

Speaking of Helldivers 2 they also added a limited reinforcement mechanic that immediately ends the mission in failure if enough players die and are forced to respawn which more often than not ends with new players that have not grinded enough to unlock perks and utilities just dying in hordes and failing missions they shouldn't even have access to yet (Seriously, put a level lock on hard missions).

Operations do offer seasonal cosmetic rewards but again, that entire system is half baked and not remotely worth the effort.

I have literally never seen a game have an Early Access period as stable and enjoyable as this game, only to become completely and utterly unplayable upon hitting 1.0. It is genuinely staggering. I am not angry or frustrated over this; I am simply [i]fascinated.[/i] It is [b]incredible[/b] how far this game has fallen. I should know; I played the Early Access so much I was [i]account level 75[/i] by the time launch happened.

For those looking to buy, here is the most important piece of information I can give: The transition to UE5 utterly destroyed this game, and it is now a nonfunctional, laggy, unplayable mess. [b]All[/b] the promising, basic but completely functional elements that were completely functional pre-engine-update are now at best buggy, at worst literally nonfunctional. Do not buy it. It does not work.

For example: Before the engine switch, you could lay mines in front of your base's walls. Enemies would then run onto the mines and explode. In my latest (and final) game [i]post[/i] engine switch, enemies spawned so close to my base that they simply never needed to run over the mines I had laid. Those mines were in a chokepoint, and were approximately three feet from our walls.

Enemies frequently no longer [i]animate[/i] when they spawn on top of you and kill you, let alone spawn where they are [i]supposed[/i] to be spawning. Previously, enemies would spawn where rumbles and spouts of flying sand appeared, letting you know that 'Look out! The enemy is coming from [i]here!'[/i] These rumbles and spouts of flying sand still exist; however, enemies will now simply pop out of the ground DIRECTLY on top of you instead, potentially [i]hundreds[/i] of feet away from where their spawn 'tell' is. And then they kill you. Because they got into melee range with you, which you're meant to avoid at all costs. But you can't, because they spawned on top of you. Because they're [b][i]not meant to do that.[/i][/b]

That is, of course... Assuming they spawn at all. Sometimes they just don't. Yes, that's correct; sometimes this Horde Shooter just has no Horde in it. Like... At all. There just isn't one. [b]Sometimes, there are just NO ENEMIES.[/b]

Exterminate objectives on the tutorial-style 'You're still learning the game, so here's a simpler version of it' Advance and Secure game mode, which could previously be done with as few as [b]two[/b] players if you [i]really[/i] knew what you were doing, now [b]almost always[/b] wipe out literally the entire game. Literally. I'm not exaggerating. Literally every single player will die. Multiple times, usually. It's bonkers.

How does that even happen? How do you go from 'These objectives work fine; enemies spawn, players kill them, maybe one or two people die, but if everyone knows to shoot the enemy with their guns and run away if something scary gets close, everyone's usually fine' to 'all of the players in the game are currently holed up inside the 999999 health superbunker with the infinite ammo locker that they respawned inside after dying to this objective, desperately shooting the bugs outside - and the bugs are [i]successfully killing the bunker.'[/i] This isn't a difficulty spike, it's [b]abnormal.[/b] It's CLEARLY [b]not supposed to work like this.[/b]

Evacuations at the end of the game, previously [i]fairly[/i] manageable, now regularly end with every player dead. Gone are the days of people pausing to bravely provide cover fire for each other on the way out, or heroically coming back to revive a fallen soldier - now, everyone simply dies. Almost immediately, in fact. Even if they don't, the performance dips down into an utterly unbelievable 1-4FPS slideshow - an unplayable quagmire that's literally shocking to look at. My PC handles newer, harsher games [i]just[/i] fine (even other UE5 ones!), so I have absolutely [i]no[/i] idea what must be going on under the hood to make this game gargle and claw at it's throat like it's swallowing broken glass. It's [i]nuts.[/i]

I knew that switching engines was a major undertaking, but this was a simple update to a newer version of the engine already in use - and yet here we are. Slack-jawed and aghast, wondering what the [b]hell[/b] even [i]happened[/i] to this game?

Sadly, there's simply no other way to say it. Helldivers 2 stands in solemn, contemplative jackbooted silence atop the corpse of this game, and the saddest part is it genuinely didn't even want OR [b]try[/b] to kill it: Starship Troopers: Extermination one day simply pulled out it's gun and just straight up [i]blew it's own brains out.[/i]

As someone who religiously played operator and prioritized ore refineries above all else, the class update has murdered the flow of ARC games. Bastion became bastion 2.0, hunter gets split into sniper (really just hunter 2.0 minus the ammo fabs) and ranger. The only thing ranger provides to the team is scanning. Other than that, it's a selfish class that gets a bunch of survivability to himself. Bastion has decent survivability, but at least he draws bugs to himself, which is super important for refinery or any point defense. Rarely do you see a ranger purposefully kiting bugs away, doing more or less the same job a guardian can do, albeit more mobile. 

And then there's the three classes that came from operator. I find it difficult to see why demolisher should even exist. What does he bring to the team? He blows up bugs rather than shooting them! Sure the nuclear charge actually has a use now for clearing bug corpses, but does that and his barrage ability really warrant a whole class for it? And why does he get to be exempt from the shit.ass ticket system when he takes watkins trigger? It's not uncommon to see demos run around outside the base to purposely die and detonate themselves over and over again. At first it did cost tickets, but people would grief with it so they came up with this? If this is the result, maybe the perk shouldn't exist at all. 

Medic is... fine. It was clear they had a hard time balancing operator's utilities, so it's good that there's a class that just specializes in healing and reviving. Engineer however, is where my biggest problem lies. The only character capable of equipping portable ammo, and inheriting the ability to carry two resource cans from operator. With those traits, surely you'd see engineers at refineries. But you don't! Because his ability, the mobile build tool, allows him to place turrets and ammo anywhere provided the terrain agrees with you. The class that gets ALL the utility, from overcharging turrets and repairing walls way faster than the other classes, to placing ammo crates outside the base and using the refined perk at refineries. So much utility in and outside the base, that in a perfect world, you'd have engineers maintaining the base, and some going out to support resource gathering. The actual engineers you find in games are the most selfish pricks imaginable, finding a nice ledge somewhere, placing a turret, and sitting on it the whole fucking game. Several matches now I've witnessed engineers who don't even bother leaving their turret to run to the extract, which brings us to another big issue with engi. They gave him all utility, and no survivability. Every class's ability helps them survive in one way or another, but not engi. Your best bet is to run a shotgun to try and keep yourself alive. So most ARC games you have guardians, demos and rangers hauling back ore, because they can actually survive. Meanwhile the actual support class is hiding on a turret on a ledge all game, providing no utility to the team. They attempted to patch the bugged build tool being able to build any structure outside the base, but you can still make a stairway to heaven out of short walls. Whenever I see that shit, I deconstruct them and watch their useless ass fall. If I were to balance the mobile build tool, I'd change it so every time an ore canister gets deposited, engis get a cut of the ore for their tool, incentivizing them to actually go and get some. I'm not saying this is a good fix, but something needs to change so engis don't kill-whore on a turret all game. Maybe remove the turret from the build options entirely and give him the sentry guns that guardian gets instead? Sentry guns are an engineer trope after all, so it's a bit weird that guardian gets them. It just feels goofy pulling ore out of your ass every 80 seconds and building whatever you want. If there was a class that could carry two cans and had an ability to help with survival, I'd take that instead in a heartbeat.

Now let's picture the average scenario of harvesting resources from when we had three classes. Hunters would be high up, providing sniper fire. Bastions would be castled up near the refinery, drawing bugs to themselves and not the latter. And operators would be reducing the cooldown on each canister, giving ammo to the bastions, and be the ones hauling back the cans. Each class had their own take on helping, and it worked really well when you had players of all classes. Sometimes I'd call out in team chat, asking for an operator to come to our refinery to help haul the stuff back, and they'd actually show up (No one ever uses voip now, if someone does it's to do some roleplay cancer). It was so simple, we'd defend the refinery, and the hunters and bastions would escort the operators back to base. Occasionally you'd get a dumbass that would take a can before the refinery went on cooldown and attempt to run it back alone. They would be met with death, every time. The average scenario for resources now is players seeing refineries as a buffet, grabbing a can and running off with it instead of helping defend until all the cans are done filling. I'll tell them to wait, but not once has it worked. They attempted to nerf ranger's boost jet while carrying a can, but it wasn't enough either. Most of the time they make it back too, because of medics in the base sending their drones out to revive them. The end result is me as an engineer, all of a sudden alone because everyone ran off with a single can, waiting to get one-shotted by a warrior. 

Another big issue I have is WHERE the refineries spawn now. I don't know if this is intentional due to only one class getting portable ammo, but most of the time the refineries spawn stupid close to the base. Agni is the worst, I only get the same base location and refinery spawns every single time. It gets so repetitive and leads to a snoozefest of a match cause both refineries are 80m away from the base. You actually got to explore the maps when making a 500m trip to get ore back then. Engi's ammo fabs get increasingly more useful the farther away from the base you go, as bug packs dwindle down a squad's ammo. Or at least it would be, if they didn't spawn so damn close now. People don't even need your ammo at this point. 

I'm leaving this review to voice my pent up frustration as most negative reviews I see are people with not even two hours of playtime, bringing up performance. Yeah it's bad, but at its core this is a team game. You have to question what each class brings to the team, when you do, some of them feel selfish and pointless. This shit just feels like a bad dream, like when speed stims first got added and totally broke the game with how hilariously fast you could run and for so long, too. They'd be too embarrassed to remove them so instead, nerfed them into being useless. However the devs seem content with these 6 classes, and with the 1.0 release of this game being announced in October of this year (much sooner than the original roadmap showed), I doubt we'll be getting any substantial class reworks.

I've been a player since week 1 of early access. Here are my thoughts.

This is THE best Starship Troopers game out there.

The gameplay loop, gun physics, and overall combat with the arachnid forces is satisfying. The side missions are interesting and bring variety to the game. Many of the mutators to the missions are great, but some of them are severe pain points. Those I will talk about first:

Mutators:
-These generally enhance either the players or the arachnids, or change the environment. Such as sandstorms, infinite utilities, more of a specific kind of bug, etc. However, part of the issue is mutator combinations leading to fully unwinnable situations. Tactics and skill should be the determining factor in whether or not the players can scratch out a win, not luck with the parameters of the mission. For example, gunners that spawn all the time that have mountains of health can lead to troopers fighting just the gunners to stay alive, which leaves all the other bugs unchecked.

Cool Concept - Poor Execution
-Perhaps it is just me, but the persistent arachnid bodies, while a cool bit that reinforces the lore (and provides a ramp for the bugs to use, a tactical challenge) and is visually striking can lead to problems. Many players don't know that they can clear those bodies, and when the bodies pile up, the game begins to lag significantly. My ping sits around 14, and I've got Tigers rubber banding at me like a yoyo, which is frustrating. A potential solution for this is to have them only pile near player structures. 

Now for some of the good bits:

I hate this planet... in a good way -- Each planet provides its own unique challenges. Valaka has a bit of everything, corners, structures, rocky formations, vertical challenges, tunnels, open spaces. Agni Prime has a bit more of a valley feel and its lava pools and foliage can provide interesting challenges. The lack of rocky formations limits cover and safe spots. X-11's tunnels and crater are unique as well, creating a central location to hunker down in, and a variety of close quarters paths for side objectives. Boreas' verticality is interesting in itself.

Gun Physics: Knowing how iron sights works improves your experience. Leading your targets increases your accuracy, especially based on distance. These are enjoyable gun physics that reward your skill level.

The result of the newest patch shows a game that feels unfinished and untested, leaving players discouraged and unable to enjoy what once showed so much potential. [h1]Don't. Simply Don't.[/h1]

I bought this game during the beta for below 25€ and we did have a lot of fun. That nonwithstanding, the current state of the game post-release is a shame and the developer should be deeply embarrassed for what they force upon their community. 
[hr][/hr]
[h2]The Pros:[/h2]

[h3]Multiplayer fun[/h3]
If you have a couple of friends to play with, rounds can be fun. They are highly repetitive, so don't expect to be challenged mentally, but the classes make sense and are diverse, and with the right type of people it's good for a lot of fun.

[h3]interesting multi-level definition of "success"[/h3]
The lobby is divided in up to 5 4-player squads (though only 16 players fit a map, don't know where this math comes from). A well-oiled squad can achieve objectives without external help, which encourages players to divide their forces, e.g. one squad defends the base while two squads independently of each other go for resources and the remains are afk or something xD

[hr][/hr]

[h2]The cons:[/h2]

[h3]The interface[/h3]
The interface has been designed someone who should ask for a refund of their tuition fee. Menu options are confusing, translations are catastrophically bad, hints - where available, such as the information that you have new weapon options - are inconsistent, don't tell you WHAAT they hint for and are buggy. You can change a squad until you choose a class, but not after. This is not told to you. Your Squad View on the left sometimes only shows 3 members, despite the Squad being full. To check who is in which squad, you need to use the 'very intuitive' key combination "TAB, then z". This is not visible anywhere in the UI. When trying to repair a building, you have around a 50% chance that left click starts the repair action. In one occasion, the game just removed any kind of HUD from my screen, which left me targetting with Iron Sights and ask others to look for my health since I had no health bar. Was kinda fun but definitely not deliberate.

[h3]Stability[/h3]
During our first session post-release we (party of 8) had
- multiple game crashes mid-mission
- 2 game crashes in the Menu
- 1 occasion where the game crashed and wouldn't start again, even after verifying, uninstalling, reinstalling, multiple reboots and essentially deleting everything but the operating system
- one kick due to cheating (no cheats were present)
- multiple kicks because of "Server closed" (the remainder of the team was able to continue playing on that server
- a broken lobby where nobody could join or be invited
- countless Lagspikes where the FPS dropped to <1
- multiple (false?) informations that the company server is currently down

[h3]Features[/h3]
The game has a lot of nice ideas, however they are sometimes implemented in a way so idiotic it beggars belief. 
1.0 introduced a new game mode that supposedly seems to be some kind of multiple-missions thing. I say supposedly because here we get to the juicy bits. In order to play this mode, you appear to have to be part of a so called "company". You have a randomly selected list of 30 companies to join, but you can also create your own. Of course we created our own - only to figure out that YOU CANNOT SEARCH FOR OR INVITE INTO a company!! Also, the suggestion dialog only offers you companies that contain at least 2 members. However since a newly formed company obviously starts with 1 member, there appears to be actually no way for us to join our own company. Whoever designed this and deemed it fit for release seriously should question his or her life's choices.

One of the more interesting features is that enemy corpses don't despawn. Instead they litter the area and eventually allow the enemy to scale walls and overrun your defenses from a vantage point. While this concept is interesting and I have to give it to the devs that they manage all this with relatively neglible impact to performance, it is BUGGY AS HELL. Frequently, you are unable to actually leave or enter a building because countless corpses and alive enemies intersect and form a solid wall. Even with this, spawnpoints are sometimes INSIDE of corpse piles, which leaves you trying to dig yourself out of that pile while enemies can selectively ignore collisions and still attack you. You can clean up the corpses with melee and some explosives. However, this is also somewhat unresponsive and seems to change between updates without any real apparent concept.

[h3]Price[/h3]
The beta was priced at around 25€. However, for release they raised the price to 50€ AND added Skin Packs on top, which brings the total tally to around 90€. This is a ridiculous entry price even for AAA games, let alone for such an unpolished bugfest (pun intended) like this game sadly became.

[h2]Conclusion[/h2]
This game had high aspirations and a very compelling theme it was set in. The idea is interesting and the core gameplay loop is fun. However, the developers in my opinion completely dropped the ball by overpromising, favoring new features over actually fixing usability bugs or even considering usability in general. Also, the 1.0 tag appears completely random, subjectively I would say the polishing of the game HEAVILY decreased between the last beta and 1.0.

Personally I do not regret having bought that game in Beta, however I [b]strongly[/b] advise anybody who made it until here against spending money on this unfinished, badly thought-through wreck of a game.

If you would have asked me a year ago if I recommended this game, I would have said absolutely, and if we were friends at the time I might have even tried to buy you a copy.

I was a fool, and had foolish hopes.

Today I learned that back in an August Q&A (about 2 months ago at time of writing) the devs said that it was too hard to separate ADS sensitivity from Hipfire sensitivity and that that feature would not come until after their 1.0 release. I was astonished by this because I have seen the exact options in the old UE4 ini files before the upgraded to UE5; they were just never activated and defined.

So I did what any nerd would do when they don't believe something and I looked into how to do it. 

At first I found a video tutorial on how to set X & Y sensitivity individually, which was something they didn't know how to do for a long time and had only 1 slider for both sensitivities. This took about 3 minutes for me to find and learn how to do, and I've never developed a game in my life (though I do have a lot of experience tweaking UE ini files).

I then refined my search and found exactly how to define input mapping contexts in UE5 and can give you a link directly to the developer guide provided by Epic.

[b]I learned how to do all of this in about 10 minutes[/b], with some minor help from Copilot, and absolutely no developer experience. [b]These 'devs' have been unable to figure out how to do this for over a year and a half.[/b]

In 8 days this game will be releasing on consoles and none of the players will be able to set different sensitivity for their hipfire versus their ADS. As someone who plays EVERYTHING (even StarCraft) with a controller, I can tell you this will make some weapons absolutely unusable and many of these would be new players are going to be turned away.

This is a game that relies heavily on an active community or it becomes unplayable. You can't finish the main co-op mode with less than an 11-12 person team. The devs knew this and that's why they rushed to put out the console version as the PC playerbase has been dwindling over the last year and a half. 

Oh did I forget to mention they are rushing out the console version ahead of their original plan?
Yea that's a thing; presumably because they need players to keep the game alive.

They also said they aren't going to allow controller controls to be customizable, at least not right away. This is not a hard thing either and a handful of us have been customizing the controls via ini edits for over a year, since they experimented several times with different controller schemes and some of them were pretty bad; and yet they can't figure out hwo to make a menu to do that, but are about to put out the full release in 8 days.

[b]If you've only skimmed this review to this point[/b] you might be thinking "this is mostly controller stuff and doesn't affect me because I'm going to use Keyboard and Mouse" but there's heavy, heavy signs of incompetence here, and rushing out 1.0 in 8 days is looking like it's going to be a disaster. Because again, these devs can't even figure out how to separate ADS from hipfire after 1.5 years, and I can teach you how to do it in less than half an hour.

And mind you, in 8 days the price is going to go up too.

I could go on longer about other poor decisions they've made (like jumping from UE4 to UE5 before they tested thoroughly) and are projected to make, but this has a character limit, and at the end of the day I simply do not recommend the game. I really, truly, wish I could because I loved this game at one point, but I respect you more than the devs have respected their fans.

I was a big fan of the old Starship Troopers game, so I was pretty excited about this one. It can be a blast if you pick the right class, have teammates with actual brains and a decent server connection and don't face any of the many below mentioned most common bugs, but that's a lot of "ifs". It's still a long way from being well playable. There are a lot of bugs that ruin the experience (no pun intended, and not talking about the ones actually attacking you).Some of the most common ones include:

- No dropship icon visible on the HUD or on the map. Go for extraction, but where to is your guess.
- Weapon positioning on the HUD being off after switching weapons. Sometimes you just see the grip and the underside of the shaft (usually you can fix this one by aiming down sights)
- Engineer turrets cannot be mounted. You can build them, but when you "use" them, nothing happens.
- Q / Ability / Cooldown not being shown. This happens pretty much every single match. Sometimes you can "fix" it by dying and respawning, but it's really annoying when you're playing something with high cooldowns like engineer and you can't see them.
- Sometimes you get hitmakers for hits but no actual points when the bug in question dies.
- Teammates not being shown in your squad list.In the lower left corner of your HUD, your teammates should be shown. But even with a full squad (4 players), you'll rarely see three other names there.
- Server issues are also common. The ping is usually pretty good, with a delay of about 1 second between "using" something and actually using it. This is already much better than your usual Overwatch experience, but there's still room for improvement. 
The building mode could be easily improved by changing the view a bit (otherwise it's really difficult to place big structures like bunkers, while small structures like wall-mounted turrets need millimeter-fine adjustments in order to be built).
- Currently, the demolisher class seems to be the worst trash ever programmed in video game history. A main weapon & a skill which deal exactly 0 damage and mobility is comparable to a pregnant whale. The only fun thing about this class is the suicide explosion, which deals about 5 damage.This class needs a complete rework or simply deletion.
- Sometimes, you cannot sprint anymore. Usually you can fix this by respawning, but not if you're playing demolisher and got the suicide explosion equipped. In  this case, you can't respawn anymore.
- Sometimes when you join a match not at the start of the mission, you are instantly killed and cannot respawn. You can still switch repsawn locations, but actually respawning is not possible.

I know the game is barely out of early access, but there is still lots and lots to do. Considering all those bugs which really ruin the game at the moment, it's definitely not worth spending 50 euros.
